case: Stab wound: tamponade, PEA and pericardiocentesis

objectives.text: – Not assessable Name the tamponade within 180 s of arrival from the monitor: tachycardia, narrow pulse pressure, CVP above 15 mmHg (instructor-assessed) This objective has no rule: the instructor judges it.
✗ Not met Start CPR within 10 s of the pulse loss CPR 14 s after the pulse loss (07:48 → 08:02; within 10 s asked).
✗ Not met Pericardiocentesis within 120 s of starting CPR The state "CPR: pericardium drained, catheter left in" 2 min 06 s after CPR (08:02 → 10:08; within 2 min 00 s asked).

✗ Not met Stop CPR (“Pulse back”) within 30 s of the pulse returning on the arterial line and the capnogram The state "Return of circulation: ventilated, catheter in the pericardium" 35 s after the return of circulation (11:44 → 12:19; within 30 s asked).
✗ Not met Better: pericardiocentesis before the pulse loss, while the systolic pressure is above 60 mmHg — then no PEA follows The pulse loss at 07:48

facts: 3 min 56 s in all; first lost at 07:48
3 min 56 s after the pulse loss (11:44)
